top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a distinct physical idea that removes the trade-off between atom number and perturbation of the clock transition, and its 10^-18 realisation is quantified, systematics-traced and reproduced across independent laboratories (RIKEN, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE). The two-name concept-plus-realisation citation is mature and attributable, and avoids reading as a mere precision record. I rank the topological-insulator trio (P003) next because the physics is mature and confirmed, though the HgTe proposal credit is unsettled and it lies outside my own expertise; the magic-angle graphene part (P002) follows because it is only about eight years old with an open pairing mechanism. No award is last because a mature, well-credited candidate exists.
